mainEntity.name: How much is a home in 94587?

acceptedAnswer.text: The typical home value in 94587 is $1,196,418 as of 2026-09-30, down 0.10 percent from the month before and down 1.9 percent over the year. That is the Zillow Home Value Index. It estimates the typical value of every home in the area, listed or not. The median asking price of what is actually on the market in ZIP 94587 is $1,249,972. Those two numbers measure different populations and they do not have to agree. For one specific house instead of the typical one, that is a comparable sales analysis, and it is a different exercise than reading an index.
94587 is in ZIP 94587, Union City, Alameda County, California.

Against the rest of Union City, yes. 94587 ranks 20 of 47 neighborhoods by typical value, and at $1,196,418 it sits 0 percent above the citywide typical value of $1,195,668. The monthly number is the one I would focus on: owning the typical home here runs about $388,097 a month once you include the loan, property tax, insurance, utilities and a maintenance budget, against a typical area rent of $2,913. The full breakdown is in the cost of holding section above.

mainEntity.name: What are property taxes in Union City?

acceptedAnswer.text: I use 1.42 percent in this report, the Alameda County effective rate. On a home at $1,196,418 that is roughly $1,416 a month, $16,989 a year. Proposition 13 sets the base at 1 percent of assessed value and caps growth in that assessed value at 2 percent a year while one owner holds the property, and voter-approved bonds sit on top. The real rate runs above 1 percent. The part that catches buyers is that a purchase resets assessed value to the price paid. Any figure you read that was built from median taxes actually paid is averaging in decades of protected assessments and will understate what a new buyer owes.

mainEntity.name: What is the transfer tax in Union City?

acceptedAnswer.text: This is the cost people forget to budget for, and it varies more by city line than anything else in a California transaction. Union City is a general law city, so the rate here is $1.10 per $1,000 of value. On a home at $1,196,418 that is $1,316. For scale, the identical sale price would carry $1,316 in Dublin and $19,262 in Oakland, both in this same county. Who pays is set by the contract and by local custom, not by statute, and it is negotiable. Escrow is the authority on the exact figure for a specific sale.

mainEntity.name: What is the FHA loan limit in Union City?

acceptedAnswer.text: For 2026 the one-unit limit in Alameda County is $1,249,125, and that figure is both the conforming conventional ceiling and the FHA ceiling. At the typical value of $1,196,418 here, a minimum-down loan of $1,154,543 fits inside the ceiling, so FHA and conforming conventional are both genuinely available. That is not true in every neighborhood in this county.

mainEntity.name: What first-time buyer help is available in Union City?

acceptedAnswer.text: CalHFA runs the statewide programs and they layer on top of a first mortgage and do not replace it. MyHome is a deferred-payment junior loan toward the down payment and closing costs, open year round. ZIP covers closing costs on a CalHFA conventional first. Dream For All is the shared-appreciation program, limited to first-generation buyers, and it runs in announced windows, not continuously. GSFA Platinum is a separate option, and Union City and Alameda County run their own programs on their own funding cycles. Those are the ones most people never hear about. The constraint that actually binds in a neighborhood at $1,196,418 is almost never income. It is the program's own purchase price cap, often set below the county loan limit. I would establish the price a program allows first, then shop inside it. Doing it the other way around is how people fall for a house the assistance cannot reach.

mainEntity.name: Can I build an ADU in Union City?

acceptedAnswer.text: Almost certainly yes, in some form. State law requires local agencies to allow accessory dwelling units on residential lots with ministerial approval and a decision deadline, so the real question is what size and configuration the local ordinance permits, not whether you are allowed. Owner-occupancy requirements on new ADUs have been removed, so the main house and the ADU can both be rented. Selling one separately is a different question. Assembly Bill 1033 lets a city allow an ADU to be sold as its own condominium unit, but it is permissive and not mandatory, relatively few cities have adopted an enabling ordinance, and without one there is no right to do it. That is a question for the Union City planning department and the municipal code, not something the state law answers on its own.

mainEntity.name: Is the Union City housing market slowing down?

acceptedAnswer.text: I would rather give you the two numbers that disagree than a verdict. Typical home value in 94587 is down 0.10 percent month over month and down 1.9 percent year over year. Meanwhile in ZIP 94587, the median asking price is down 3.8 percent year over year, price per square foot is down 3.7 percent, active listings are up 19.6 percent month over month, and median days on market is down 2.1 percent. More supply and a slower pace sitting alongside a higher typical value is a composition effect, not a contradiction. Anyone giving you a one-word answer about a market this specific is not looking at it closely.

The Zillow Observed Rent Index for ZIP 94587 is $2,913 as of 2026-09-30, up 7.8 percent over the year. I use that figure in the cost of waiting section to show what renting while you decide actually costs over two and five years, because that is the real comparison and it usually goes unmade.

mainEntity.name: How many homes are for sale in 94587?

acceptedAnswer.text: In ZIP 94587 as of 2026-09 there were 61 active listings, up 19.6 percent from the prior month and up 24.5 percent from a year earlier. That month saw 40 new that month and 22 pending. Median days on market was 35.

mainEntity.name: How much is home insurance in Union City?

acceptedAnswer.text: I use $215 a month, $2,580 a year, the California statewide average. A real quote on a specific house moves with the structure, the roof, the replacement cost and the wildfire risk rating on the parcel, so treat the average as a placeholder until you have a quote. One thing worth flagging: a vacant home is a different and more expensive class of policy. That catches sellers who move out before closing, and it catches estates almost every time.

mainEntity.name: What is it like living in 94587?

On the money side, typical value is $1,196,418, the monthly carry is around $388,097, and rent runs $2,913.
